Bill to merge SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore into a new Skills and Workforce Development Agency

Second Reading5 May 2026 bill-794, bill-795, bill-796

A Bill at Second Reading to establish the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) by merging SkillsFuture Singapore and Workforce Singapore and transferring their functions, employees and assets.

The Bill establishes SWDA as a statutory board whose functions cover the existing functions of SSG and WSG and extend to promoting career and employment services and training. If passed, SWDA will be established in the third quarter of 2026, and employees of WSG and SSG will transfer on terms no less favourable than their present ones. The Minister said SSG's and WSG's operations will be fully undertaken by SWDA from Day One, with existing grant and employment assistance commitments honoured.

  • Will the Government appoint a bridging political office holder for Manpower and Education?
  • Will SWDA directly provide job search assistance or rely on third parties?
  • Will SWDA require job assistance programmes to guide jobseekers on technical skills and proactive pitching?
  • Will SWDA work directly with schools to provide systematic career guidance at lower secondary level?
  • Will university and polytechnic admissions expand aptitude-based admissions?
  • Will SWDA publish outcome-based figures annually?
  • Will SWDA track and publish median time to employment by age band, PMET status and service provider?
  • Will SWDA review the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme's salary cap and criteria for involuntary unemployment?
  • Will SWDA require anti-discrimination risk assessments for AI-enabled HR technology?
  • Will SWDA commit to tracking and posting statistics on adoption of skills-based hiring by employers?
  • Will SWDA merge MySkillsFuture and MyCareersFuture portals?
  • Will SWDA compensate training providers for trainees who do not pass?
  • Will SWDA set up a formal no wrong door protocol and published service standards?
  • Will SWDA define the role of NTUC and e2i in the new structure?
  • Will SWDA have a single complaints and appeals pathway?
  • Will SWDA track wage progression, job stability and well-being?
  • Will SWDA support gig workers, freelancers and informal care roles?
  • Will SWDA expand place-and-train programmes?
  • Will SWDA consider a further tranche of SkillsFuture credit?
  • Will SWDA review SkillsFuture credit caps?
  • Will SWDA track performance of Jobs Nearby @ CDC?
  • Will SWDA publish data on public service job postings with or without academic requirements?
  • Will SWDA set up advisory panels or sector-specific councils?
  • Will SWDA retain sector-specific expertise?
  • Will SWDA establish regular ongoing engagement with stakeholders?

Motion on AI-enabled growth and support for workers and enterprises

5 May 2026 – 6 May 2026 motion-2970, motion-2976, motion-2978

A Motion moved by Mr Ng Chee Meng setting out four commitments on AI-enabled economic growth, fairness, worker and enterprise support, and inclusive progress, followed by debate and a ministerial response.

The transcript sets out measures that affect workers and businesses: from the second half of this year, Singaporeans enrolled in selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools; eligible businesses will receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit later this year; and all IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses for alumni at a significant discount for a year starting in the second half of this year. It also records that the Government will study improvements to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme and that tripartite partners are discussing shortening retrenchment notification under the Employment Act review.
